setUV() and setUVPixels() are just simpler ways of setting this matrix
omni-morph.docs.model_part.get_uv_matrix: Gets the UV matrix of this part
omni-morph.docs.model_part.set_color:
Sets the color multiplier for this part for primary and secondary colors
Values are RGB from 0 to 1
omni-morph.docs.model_part.get_color:
Returns the average set color from this part, as adding the primary color with the secondary, then dividing them
Values are RGB from 0 to 1
omni-morph.docs.model_part.set_primary_c:
Sets the primary color multiplier for this part
Values are RGB from 0 to 1
omni-morph.docs.model_part.get_primary_c:
Gets the primary color multiplier of this part
Values are RGB from 0 to 1
omni-morph.docs.model_part.set_secondary:
Sets the secondary color multiplier for this part
Values are RGB from 0 to 1
omni-morph.docs.model_part.get_secondary:
Gets the secondary color multiplier of this part
Values are RGB from 0 to 1
omni-morph.docs.model_part.set_opacity:
Sets the opacity multiplier of this part
Note that opacity settings will only take effect if the part has a suitable Render Type for them, mainly TRANSLUCENT
Check out modelPart.setPrimaryRenderType() for how to do this
omni-morph.docs.model_part.get_opacity:
Gets the opacity multiplier of this part
Note that opacity settings will only take effect if the part has a suitable Render Type for them, mainly TRANSLUCENT
Check out modelPart.setPrimaryRenderType() for how to do this
omni-morph.docs.model_part.set_light:
Sets the light level to be used when rendering this part
Values you give are 0 to 15, indicating the block light and sky light levels you want to use
Passing nil will reset the lighting override for this part
omni-morph.docs.model_part.get_light:
Gets the light level you set earlier to this part
Does not interact with Minecraft's lighting system, only retrieving values you set earlier with setLight()
omni-morph.docs.model_part.set_overlay:
Sets the overlay color to be used when rendering this part
Values you give are 0 to 15, indicating the white overlay and the damage overlay levels you want to use
Passing nil will reset the overlay override for this part
omni-morph.docs.model_part.get_overlay:
Gets the overlay color you set earlier to this part
Does not interact with Minecraft's overlay system, only retrieving values you set earlier with setOverlay()
omni-morph.docs.model_part.set_parent_ty:
Sets the parent type of the part
See the ParentType parts in the list docs for legal types
omni-morph.docs.model_part.get_parent_ty: Returns the current parent type of the part
omni-morph.docs.model_part.get_type: Returns whether this part is a "GROUP", a "CUBE", or a "MESH"
omni-morph.docs.model_part.override_vani: Returns if this part vanilla rotation is being overridden by an animation
Returns if this part vanilla position is being overridden by an animation
Returns if this part vanilla scale is being overridden by an animation
omni-morph.docs.model_part.new_text: Adds a new Text Render Task on this part
omni-morph.docs.model_part.new_item: Adds a new Item Render Task on this part
omni-morph.docs.model_part.new_block: Adds a new Block Render Task on this part
omni-morph.docs.model_part.new_sprite: Adds a new Sprite Render Task on this part
omni-morph.docs.model_part.new_entity: Adds a new Entity Render Task on this part
omni-morph.docs.model_part.add_task: Adds the given Render Task on this part
omni-morph.docs.model_part.get_task:
Gets the Render Task with the given name from this part
Returns a table with all tasks if a name is not given
omni-morph.docs.model_part.remove_task:
Removes the Task with the given name from this part
Removes ALL tasks if a name is not given
omni-morph.docs.model_part.remove: Removes this part from the parent model part
omni-morph.docs.model_part.get_vertices:
Return a table with all vertices from the given texture id
Returns nil if no vertices were found
omni-morph.docs.model_part.get_all_verti: Return a table of all texture ids and their vertices
omni-morph.docs.model_part.move_to: Moves this part to be a child of the given part
omni-morph.docs.model_part.add_child: Adds the given part into this part's children list
omni-morph.docs.model_part.remove_child: Removes the given part from this part's children list
omni-morph.docs.model_part.copy:
Returns a copy of this part, with all customizations and vertices copied
Children parts are passed as reference, in a new list
omni-morph.docs.model_part.new_part:
Creates a new, empty, group model part as a child of this part, at the same pivot point
Takes two arguments, the new part's name, and optionally its parent type
omni-morph.docs.nameplate: A global API which is used for customizing your player's nameplate in chat, above your head, and in the tab list
omni-morph.docs.nameplate.chat: A customization for your nameplate in the chat
omni-morph.docs.nameplate.entity: A customization for your nameplate above your head
omni-morph.docs.nameplate.list: A customization for your nameplate in the tab list
omni-morph.docs.nameplate.all: A group that manages all your nameplate customizations at once
omni-morph.docs.nameplate_customization: A customization that can be applied to a nameplate
The text to use in this nameplate
The text to use in this nameplate
omni-morph.docs.nameplate_entity: A nameplate customization that is specialized for entities
omni-morph.docs.nameplate_entity.get_piv: Gets the pivot of the nameplate, in world coordinates
omni-morph.docs.nameplate_entity.set_piv: Sets the pivot of the nameplate, in world coordinates

omni-morph.docs.raycast.aabb:
Raycasts based on a start position, an end position, and an array of Axis Aligned Bounding Boxes defined by the player.
AABBs are encoded as a table with indicies 1 and 2 being a Vector3.
`{vec(0,0,0),vec(1,0.5,1)}` is a valid AABB, with `{ {vec(0,0,0),vec(1,0.5,1)}, {vec(0,0.5,0.5),vec(1,1,1)} }` being a valid AABB array.
This function returns the AABB table that was hit, the exact position hit as a Vector3, the side of the AABB hit as a string or nil if inside an AABB, and the index of the AABB that was hit in the array
omni-morph.docs.raycast.block:
Raycasts a Block in the world.
If successful, returns the BlockState hit, the exact world position hit as a Vector3, and the side of the block that was hit.
When unsuccessful, returns nil.
blockCastType and fluidCastType determine how the raycast handles block shapes and fluids.
Will default to "COLLIDER" and "NONE" when nil
omni-morph.docs.raycast.entity:
Raycasts an Entity in the world
If successful, returns the EntityAPI hit and the exact world position hit as a Vector3.
When unsuccessful, returns nil.
predicate is a function that prevents specific entities from being raycasted.
Takes in a single EntityAPI object. Return true for valid entities, false for invalid.
Marks all entities as valid when nil

omni-morph.docs.vectors.int_to_rgb: Converts the given color from Integer format to RGB format

A vector that holds 2 numbers

omni-morph.docs.vector3:

omni-morph.docs.vector4:

omni-morph.docs.vector_n.sub: Subtracts the given vector or values from this one, and returns self for chaining
omni-morph.docs.vector_n.offset: Offsets this vector by the given factor, adding the factor to all components, and returns self for chaining
omni-morph.docs.vector_n.mul: Multiplies the given vector or values into this one, and returns self for chaining
omni-morph.docs.vector_n.div: Divides this vector by the given vector or values, and returns self for chaining

Returns the length of this vector squared
Suitable when you only care about relative lengths, because it avoids a square root
omni-morph.docs.vector_n.copy: Creates and returns a copy of this vector
omni-morph.docs.vector_n.dot: Returns the dot product of this vector with the other
omni-morph.docs.vector_n.normalize:
Modifies this vector so that its length is 1 unless its length was originally 0
Returns self for chaining
omni-morph.docs.vector_n.normalized: Returns a copy of this vector with length 1 unless its length was originally 0
omni-morph.docs.vector_n.clamp_length:
Modifies this vector so that its length is between minLength and maxLength
If the vector has length zero, it is unmodified
Returns self for chaining
omni-morph.docs.vector_n.clamped:
Returns a modified copy of this vector, with its length clamped from minLength to maxLength
If the vector has length zero, then the copy does too
omni-morph.docs.vector_n.length: Returns the length of this vector
omni-morph.docs.vector_n.to_rad: Returns a copy of this vector, in radians
omni-morph.docs.vector_n.to_deg: Returns a copy of this vector, in degrees
omni-morph.docs.vector_n.floor: Returns a copy of this vector with its values rounded down
omni-morph.docs.vector_n.ceil: Returns a copy of this vector with its values rounded up
omni-morph.docs.vector_n.apply_func:
Calls the given function on each element of this vector, and sets the values of the vector to the returns
The current index and its value is given as arguments of the function
Returns self for chaining

Returns the augmented form of this vector
The augmented form is a Vector of the same length + 1
The new axis will have the given value, or 1 when it is not specified
